name: Mahlah
title: Daughter of Zelophehad Who Fought for Women's Inheritance Rights
summary: Mahlah was the eldest of Zelophehad's five daughters from the tribe of Manasseh. When their father died without sons, the brave sisters approached Moses and the leaders to claim inheritance rights to their father's land allotment. Their case led to important legislation that secured inheritance rights for daughters when there were no sons.

keyEvents.title: Zelophehad's Daughters Present Their Case Before Moses
keyEvents.description: Mahlah and her sisters approached Moses, the priest Eleazar, and the entire congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to claim inheritance rights after their father, who had died in the wilderness without leaving any sons.

keyEvents.title: The Lord Grants Mahlah and Her Sisters Justice
keyEvents.description: God answered Moses and confirmed that the daughters of Zelophehad were right. They were to receive their father's land allotment as an inheritance, and this became a new law for all Israel.

keyEvents.title: New Inheritance Law for Israel
keyEvents.description: Through the case of Mahlah and her sisters, the Lord established a general inheritance law: If a man dies without sons, his inheritance shall pass to his daughters.

keyEvents.title: The Question of Marriage Within the Tribe
keyEvents.description: The leaders of the tribe of Manasseh expressed concern that the land allotment might pass to other tribes if the daughters married outside their own tribe. Moses gave the command that they must marry within their father's tribe.

keyEvents.title: Mahlah and Her Sisters Marry Within the Tribe of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: Mahlah and her sisters obeyed the Lord's command and married men from the tribe of Manasseh, so that the inheritance remained within the tribe.

keyEvents.title: Mahlah Mentioned in the Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Mahlah and her sisters are recorded in the genealogical lists as the daughters of Zelophehad in the tribe of Manasseh, and they received their land allotment in the land of Canaan.
